task: Choose the correct form: My bag is ___ than your bag.
wrong options / checks: heavy | more heavy | heavyer
explanation shown to learner: *Heavy* ends in *-y*: *heavy → heavier*, then *than*.
explanation in Latvian: *Heavy* beidzas ar *-y*: *heavy → heavier*, pēc tam *than*.

task: Choose the correct word: This film is ___ than the book.
wrong options / checks: gooder | more good | best
explanation shown to learner: *Good* is irregular: *good → better*.
explanation in Latvian: *Good* ir neregulārs: *good → better*.

task: Choose the correct form: Anna is the ___ girl in our class.
wrong options / checks: taller | most tall | more tall
explanation shown to learner: With one-syllable words: *the* + adjective + *-est*: *the tallest*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar vienas zilbes vārdiem: *the* + īpašības vārds + *-est*: *the tallest*.

task: Choose the correct form: Our flat is ___ than their flat.
wrong options / checks: more new | newest | new than
explanation shown to learner: Short adjective: *new → newer*, then *than*.
explanation in Latvian: Īss īpašības vārds: *new → newer*, pēc tam *than*.

task: Choose the correct word: Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
wrong options / checks: a | more | most
explanation shown to learner: We use *the* before a superlative: *the highest*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirms vispārākās pakāpes lieto *the*: *the highest*.

task: Which sentence compares two things?
correct answer: My car is smaller than yours.
wrong options / checks: My car is the smallest in the street. | My car is very small. | My car is small and red.
explanation shown to learner: *Smaller than* compares two things.
explanation in Latvian: *Smaller than* salīdzina divas lietas.

task: A bus is ___ than a taxi. (cheap)
explanation shown to learner: One syllable: *cheap + -er = cheaper*.
explanation in Latvian: Viena zilbe: *cheap + -er = cheaper*.

task: Today is ___ than yesterday. (hot)
explanation shown to learner: Short word ending in vowel + consonant: double the last letter: *hot → hotter*.
explanation in Latvian: Īss vārds, kas beidzas ar patskani un līdzskani: dubulto pēdējo burtu: *hot → hotter*.

task: This is the ___ cake in the shop. (big)
explanation shown to learner: Double the last letter: *big → the biggest*.
explanation in Latvian: Dubulto pēdējo burtu: *big → the biggest*.

task: She is ___ student in our group. (good)
explanation shown to learner: The superlative of *good* is *the best*.
explanation in Latvian: *Good* vispārākā pakāpe ir *the best*.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She is more tall than her brother.
wrong options / checks: She is taller than her brother. | He is the youngest in the family. | This bag is lighter than that one.
explanation shown to learner: One-syllable adjectives take *-er*: *taller*, not *more tall*.
explanation in Latvian: Vienas zilbes īpašības vārdiem pievieno *-er*: *taller*, nevis *more tall*.

task: Write one sentence with older and than: Tom is twelve. Ben is ten.
correct answer: Tom is older than Ben. | Tom is two years older than Ben. | Tom is older than Ben is.
explanation shown to learner: Compare with *older than*: *Tom is older than Ben.*
explanation in Latvian: Salīdzini ar *older than*: *Tom is older than Ben.*

task: Put the words in order.
explanation shown to learner: Subject + *is* + comparative + *than* + the other thing.
explanation in Latvian: Teikuma teik. priekšmets + *is* + pārākā pakāpe + *than + otra lieta*.

task: Match each adjective with its comparative.
correct answer: big = bigger ; happy = happier ; nice = nicer ; good = better
explanation shown to learner: Spelling changes: *big → bigger*, *happy → happier*, *nice → nicer*; *good* is irregular.
explanation in Latvian: Pareizrakstības izmaiņas: *big → bigger, happy → happier, nice → nicer; good* ir neregulārs.

task: Choose the correct form: This exercise is ___ than the last one.
wrong options / checks: difficulter | most difficult | more difficulter
explanation shown to learner: Long adjectives take *more*: *more difficult than*.
explanation in Latvian: Gariem īpašības vārdiem lieto *more*: *more difficult than*.

task: Choose the correct form: My phone is ___ yours: they both cost 300 euros.
wrong options / checks: more expensive than | the most expensive | as expensive than
explanation shown to learner: *as ... as* says two things are equal.
explanation in Latvian: *as* ... *as* parāda, ka divas lietas ir vienādas.

task: Choose the correct word: She is the tallest girl ___ her class.
wrong options / checks: of | from | than
explanation shown to learner: After a superlative we use *in* + a place or group: *in her class*.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz vispārākās pakāpes lieto *in + vieta* vai grupa: *in her class*.

task: Choose the correct word: My shoes are the same ___ yours.
wrong options / checks: than | like | to
explanation shown to learner: We say *the same as*.
explanation in Latvian: Saka *the same as*.

task: Which sentence means the same as 'My room is bigger than yours'?
correct answer: Your room is smaller than mine.
wrong options / checks: Your room is bigger than mine. | Your room is as big as mine. | Your room is the smallest.
explanation shown to learner: If my room is bigger, yours is smaller.
explanation in Latvian: Ja mana istaba ir lielāka, tava ir mazāka.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: This is the more interesting book in the shop.
wrong options / checks: This book is more interesting than that one. | This is the most interesting book in the shop. | That book is as interesting as this one.
explanation shown to learner: For three or more things we use *the most*, not *the more*.
explanation in Latvian: Trim vai vairāk lietām lieto *the most*, nevis *the more*.

task: Gold is ___ than silver. (expensive)
explanation shown to learner: Long adjective: *more expensive than*.
explanation in Latvian: Garš īpašības vārds: *more expensive than*.

task: This is ___ film I have ever seen. (bad)
explanation shown to learner: The superlative of *bad* is *the worst*.
explanation in Latvian: *Bad* vispārākā pakāpe ir *the worst*.

task: The train is ___ than the bus. (fast)
explanation shown to learner: One syllable: *fast + -er = faster*.
explanation in Latvian: Viena zilbe: *fast + -er = faster*.

task: Rewrite with not as ... as: Tom is taller than Sam.
correct answer: Sam is not as tall as Tom. | Sam isn't as tall as Tom.
explanation shown to learner: *not as ... as* says one is less: *Sam is not as tall as Tom.*
explanation in Latvian: *not as* ... *as* nozīmē mazāk: *Sam is not as tall as Tom.*

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: this jacket is cheaper than that one
explanation shown to learner: Subject + *is* + comparative + *than* + *that one*.
explanation in Latvian: teik. priekšmets + *is* + pārākā pakāpe + *than + that one*.

task: Match each adjective with its superlative.
correct answer: long = the longest ; easy = the easiest ; expensive = the most expensive ; bad = the worst
explanation shown to learner: *-est* for short words, *the most* for long words, and irregular *the worst*.
explanation in Latvian: *-est* īsiem vārdiem, *the most* gariem vārdiem un neregulārais *the worst*.

task: Choose the correct option: The new hotel is ___ more comfortable than the old one, so we will stay there again.
wrong options / checks: very | too | more
explanation shown to learner: *much* + comparative shows a big difference: *much more comfortable*.
explanation in Latvian: *much* + pārākā pakāpe parāda lielu atšķirību: *much more comfortable*.

task: Choose the correct option: Travelling by train is a bit ___ than driving, but it is more relaxing.
wrong options / checks: more slow | slowest | the slower
explanation shown to learner: *a bit* + comparative shows a small difference: *a bit slower*.
explanation in Latvian: *a bit* + pārākā pakāpe parāda nelielu atšķirību: *a bit slower*.

task: Choose the correct option: She works ___ than her colleagues, so she often finishes late.
wrong options / checks: more hard | hardest | hardly
explanation shown to learner: *Hard* is also an adverb: *hard → harder*.
explanation in Latvian: *Hard* ir arī apstākļa vārds: *hard → harder*.

task: Choose the correct option: Of all the students, Maria speaks English ___ .
wrong options / checks: more fluently | the more fluent | most fluent
explanation shown to learner: Adverbs ending in *-ly* use *the most*: *the most fluently*.
explanation in Latvian: Apstākļa vārdiem ar *-ly* lieto *the most*: *the most fluently*.

task: Which sentence says the difference is small?
correct answer: This bag is slightly bigger than that one.
wrong options / checks: This bag is much bigger than that one. | This bag is far bigger than that one. | This bag is the biggest in the shop.
explanation shown to learner: *slightly* and *a bit* show a small difference; *much* and *far* show a big one.
explanation in Latvian: *slightly* un *a bit* parāda nelielu atšķirību; *much* un *far* - lielu.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: The weather today is much more warmer than yesterday.
wrong options / checks: The weather today is much warmer than yesterday. | It was the coldest day of the whole winter. | It is not as cold as it was last week.
explanation shown to learner: We use *warmer* or *more*, never both: *much warmer*.
explanation in Latvian: Lieto *warmer* vai *more*, nekad abus: *much warmer*.

task: Prices in the city centre are far ___ than in the suburbs. (high)
explanation shown to learner: *far* + comparative: *far higher*.
explanation in Latvian: *far* + pārākā pakāpe: *far higher*.

task: This printer is ___ expensive than the other one, so I think we should buy it.
explanation shown to learner: *less ... than* is the opposite of *more ... than*.
explanation in Latvian: *less* ... *than* ir pretējs *more* ... *than*.

task: Rewrite with less ... than: This flat is more expensive than that flat.
correct answer: That flat is less expensive than this flat. | That flat is less expensive than this one.
explanation shown to learner: Turn it round with *less ... than*: *That flat is less expensive than this flat.*
explanation in Latvian: Apgriez ar *less* ... *than*: *That flat is less expensive than this flat.*

task: Rewrite with as ... as: My brother and I are both 1.80 metres tall.
correct answer: My brother is as tall as I am. | My brother is as tall as me. | I am as tall as my brother. | I'm as tall as my brother.
explanation shown to learner: Equal size: *as tall as*.
explanation in Latvian: Vienāds garums: *as tall as*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: this job is much more stressful than my last one
explanation shown to learner: *much* + *more* + adjective + *than* shows a big difference.
explanation in Latvian: *much + more* + īpašības vārds + *than* parāda lielu atšķirību.

task: Match each sentence with its meaning.
correct answer: The new phone is much faster. = a big difference ; The new phone is a bit faster. = a small difference ; The new phone is not as fast. = the old one is faster ; The new phone is the fastest. = no other phone is faster
explanation shown to learner: *much* = big difference, *a bit* = small difference, *not as ... as* = less, *the fastest* = top of the group.
explanation in Latvian: *much = liela* atšķirība, *a bit = maza* atšķirība, *not as* ... *as* = mazāk, *the fastest* = labākais grupā.
replaces: The new phone is much = faster than the old one. ; The new phone is a bit = heavier than the old one. ; The new phone is not as = cheap as the old one. ; The new phone is the = best one in the shop.

task: Choose the correct option: It is the ___ meal I have ever eaten.
wrong options / checks: better | most good | goodest
explanation shown to learner: With *ever* we use a superlative: *the best meal I have ever eaten*.
explanation in Latvian: Ar *ever* lieto vispārāko pakāpi: *the best meal I have ever eaten*.

task: Choose the correct option: The more I practise, ___ I feel.
wrong options / checks: more confident | the most confident | the confident
explanation shown to learner: *The more ..., the more ...* shows two things that change together.
explanation in Latvian: *The more ..., the more* ... parāda divas lietas, kas mainās kopā.

task: It is getting ___ and ___ every day. (cold)
explanation shown to learner: *Getting colder and colder* shows a change that continues.
explanation in Latvian: *Getting colder and colder* parāda pārmaiņu, kas turpinās.

task: Their new office is twice ___ big as the old one.
explanation shown to learner: We say *twice as big as*.
explanation in Latvian: Saka *twice as big as*.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: He is by far the more experienced player in the team.
wrong options / checks: He is by far the most experienced player in the team. | She is twice as old as her cousin. | Their house is not as big as ours.
explanation shown to learner: A group of three or more needs *the most experienced*.
explanation in Latvian: Grupai no trim vai vairāk vajag *the most experienced*.

task: Rewrite with the superlative: No other mountain in this country is as high as Mount Hill.
correct answer: Mount Hill is the highest mountain in this country. | Mount Hill is the highest mountain in the country.
explanation shown to learner: If nothing is higher, it is *the highest*.
explanation in Latvian: Ja nekas nav augstāks, tas ir *the highest*.

task: What is the difference between 'This book is more interesting than that one' and 'This book is as interesting as that one'?
correct answer: The first says one is better; the second says they are equal.
wrong options / checks: The first says they are equal; the second says one is better. | Both sentences say the same. | The first is about the past; the second is about the future.
explanation shown to learner: *more ... than* shows a difference; *as ... as* shows equal.
explanation in Latvian: *more* ... *than* parāda atšķirību; *as* ... *as* - vienādību.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: this year was not as busy as last year
explanation shown to learner: *not as busy as* says last year was busier.
explanation in Latvian: *not as busy as* nozīmē, ka pērn bija vairāk darba.

task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: My English is better than last year.
wrong options / checks: My English is more good than last year. | My English is the best than last year. | My English is gooder than last year.
explanation shown to learner: *Better* is already a comparative: no *more*.
explanation in Latvian: *Better* jau ir pārākā pakāpe: bez *more*.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: this flat is not as bright as the one we saw yesterday
explanation shown to learner: *not as ... as* says the first thing has less of the quality.
explanation in Latvian: *not as* ... *as* nozīmē, ka *pirmajam* ir mazāk šīs īpašības.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: the more you practise the better you get
explanation shown to learner: *The more ..., the better ...* shows two things that change together.
explanation in Latvian: *The more ..., the better* ... parāda divas lietas, kas mainās kopā.

task: The new model is much ___ than the old one. (reliable)
wrong options / checks: bank: more reliable | reliabler | most reliable
explanation shown to learner: Long adjective: *more reliable than*.
explanation in Latvian: Garš īpašības vārds: *more reliable than*.

task: Match each comparison with its meaning.
correct answer: twice as expensive as = costs double ; not as big as = smaller ; slightly cheaper than = a little less money ; by far the best = much better than all the others
explanation shown to learner: *Twice as ... as*, *not as ... as*, *slightly* and *by far* show how big the difference is.
explanation in Latvian: *Twice as* ... *as, not as* ... *as, slightly* un *by far* parāda, cik *liela* ir atšķirība.
